answer: In an agent market for quartz, each seller must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before its offers become visible, and each bond can back only one active identity. A gale of new accounts therefore brings no free selling capacity: an attacker can forge names, but operating 10,000 sellers requires locking $1 million. The defense makes identities costly through tied-up capital and financing costs, though a wealthy attacker can still pay.
